top3.headline: Perplexity says Teammate agent hours grew 11x in a week
top3.whyItMatters: Workplace agent use can compound in weeks, so track hours saved, not seats bought.

top3.headline: Vercel CEO outlines how agents can ship code safely
top3.whyItMatters: Agent output needs feature flags, automated checks and live metrics before it reaches customers.

top3.headline: ChatGPT Wallet lets OpenAI's agents buy things for users
top3.whyItMatters: Agent payments are reaching mainstream apps, so decide how your business handles agent buyers.

items.title: Meng To builds a Dark Souls-style browser game in 3 days
items.takeaway: He used Three.js, Fable 5.2 and Opus 5.5 in Claude Code, Seedream 5.0 Pro and Tripo 3D, and shared prompts in a 10-part thread.
items.soWhat: Small teams can now prototype 3D game ideas in days, with the workflow public.

items.title: Rauch: two prompts built a framework-free UI with Gemini Argon
items.takeaway: Using fx and Gemini Argon, the agent produced a pure Web Components interface and reused 14 UI SDK behaviors, from window dragging to typeahead.
items.soWhat: Agents can assemble complex interfaces without a framework when given a library of reusable behaviors.

items.title: Perplexity says Teammate agent hours grew 11x in a week
items.takeaway: Aravind Srinivas says weekly agent hours rose 11x after 7x the week before, and staff gaining an extra workday more than tripled since September.
items.soWhat: Workplace agent use can compound in weeks, so track hours saved, not seats bought.

items.title: Rauch: agents can ship behind feature flags and watch metrics
items.takeaway: Guillermo Rauch describes agents writing feature-gated code, verification gates on push for proof checks and security audits, then the agent monitoring metrics.
items.soWhat: Safe agent shipping rests on gates and monitoring, not on trusting the model.

items.title: Simon Willison: Claude's auto mode may refuse some actions
items.takeaway: Simon Willison says regular Claude chat now runs in auto mode and may refuse actions; he prompts a session-level permission grant.
items.soWhat: Agent safety checks will sometimes block real work, so teach teams how to grant permission.

items.title: Tavi Costa: the US-China yield gap is the key macro divergence
items.takeaway: He shares a chart of US and China 10-year yields and calls the gap the most important divergence between two superpowers funding an AI arms race.
items.soWhat: Borrowing costs shape how long each superpower can keep funding its AI build-out.

items.title: Nathan Benaich: AI infrastructure security is increasingly precarious
items.takeaway: Nathan Benaich says inference providers and their bare-metal suppliers are increasingly precarious on security, and sees room for a company to fix it.
items.soWhat: Ask your inference vendors how they secure the hardware layer beneath your models.

items.title: Meng To shares a 3D workflow using Tripo3D, Blender and Claude
items.takeaway: From Kamome Ashizawa's write-up: give Claude three reference images and a backstory, with CLAUDE.md and planning subagents.
items.soWhat: 3D asset work now runs through agent harnesses, not only modeling tools.

items.title: Garry Tan: Fable 5.2 costs 2.8x more per solved coding task
items.takeaway: On 52 Claude Code tasks, Fable 5.2 solved 82.7% vs 84.6% for Opus 5.5, at 2.80x the cost per solved task.
items.soWhat: Keep the cheaper model as default until harder tasks show a real gap.

items.title: T3 Code lets agents restyle the app's interface on the fly
items.takeaway: Theo says T3 Code users can ask their agent to change the UI and see it update live.
items.soWhat: Self-customizing tools let teams shape software by request instead of by ticket.

items.title: Replit CEO says Visa agentic commerce work will expand
items.takeaway: Amjad Masad says partnering with Visa on agentic commerce has gone well, with more features and use cases coming.
items.soWhat: Payment networks are building rails for agents to buy, so plan controls on agent spending.

items.title: Cursor publishes its security incident report and remediation steps
items.takeaway: Cursor posted an update on its recent security incident, with an overview of what happened and its remediation steps.
items.soWhat: Teams using Cursor should read the report and confirm the fixes cover their setup.

items.title: Claude Code Projects get a more proactive coordinator
items.takeaway: In a project, Claude coordinates tasks across parallel threads and now answers questions and posts status updates.
items.soWhat: Leaders can follow parallel agent work in one project chat instead of checking each thread.

items.title: ChatGPT Wallet lets OpenAI's Dots agents make purchases
items.takeaway: The Verge reports ChatGPT Wallet lets OpenAI's Dots agents buy things for users.
items.soWhat: Agents that can pay will reach your checkout, so decide how you serve them.

items.title: Stratechery publishes 'The End of Jensen' on Nvidia's transition
items.takeaway: Stratechery and The Verge publish analysis of Jensen Huang's exit as Nvidia CEO.
items.soWhat: Most AI compute plans rest on Nvidia, so its leadership change deserves a close watch.

items.title: LangChain raises $300M at a $3B valuation
items.takeaway: LangChain says more than 7,000 companies use LangSmith for agent runtime, improvement and governance.
items.soWhat: Agent tooling vendors are scaling fast; check lock-in before your agent stack standardizes on one.

items.title: Wiz CTO: AI runs in 20 minutes attacks that took weeks
items.takeaway: Ami Luttwak says companies must keep attacking their own systems with the latest models.
items.soWhat: Budget for continuous AI red-teaming; yearly penetration tests no longer match attacker speed.

items.title: Peter Steinberger's team writes up OpenAI's persistent agents
items.takeaway: He says his team wrote about how they run persistent agents inside OpenAI; his post links the write-up.
items.soWhat: A frontier lab's own operating notes are a rare benchmark for your agent setup.

items.title: Simon Willison: Gemini 4 Carbon and Argon prices double Dec 1
items.takeaway: Argon and Carbon share one token price; the new Hydrogen is only a 25% discount on it.
items.soWhat: Teams running agents on Gemini 4 should re-cost those workloads before December.

items.title: Ray Dalio: let someone else measure your progress
items.takeaway: Ideally someone other than you measures and reports your progress; missed targets are a separate problem to diagnose.
items.soWhat: Independent measurement keeps leaders honest; assign it outside the team that owns the target.

items.title: Anthropic files its IPO registration with the SEC
items.takeaway: Anthropic says it has filed a registration statement, including a prospectus, for its initial public offering.
items.soWhat: A public Anthropic will disclose costs and risks; read the prospectus before your next model contract.

voices.quote: On 52 coding tasks in Claude Code 2.1.322, Fable 5.2 solved about as many (82.7% vs 84.6%) but cost 2.80x as much per solved task.
We’ve published an update on our recent security incident.
T3 Code now lets you fully customize your UI in app. Ask your agent to make changes and it will update on the fly
In a project, Claude coordinates your tasks across parallel threads. The coordinator is now much more proactive.

hotOnX.text: A nontechnical T3 Code user asked her agent for a nightly-only feature; it cloned the source and put her on a fork.
hotOnX.note: Shows an agent taking a big step for a nontechnical user unprompted.

hotOnX.text: Two prompts with fx and Gemini Argon produced a pure Web Components UI, reusing 14 UI SDK behaviors.
hotOnX.note: Builders want proof agents can make real interfaces without a framework.

hotOnX.text: Agent writes feature-gated code, verification gates run on push, agent monitors metrics. Doable today with Vercel CLI.
hotOnX.note: A concrete answer to how teams let agents ship without breaking things.

hotOnX.text: Claude chat now uses auto mode and may refuse to run things; granting permission in a message unblocked it.
hotOnX.note: 229 replies show many users hitting the same new refusals.

hotOnX.text: US vs China 10-year yields: probably the most important macro divergence between two superpowers in an AI arms race.
hotOnX.note: Investors are tying bond markets to the cost of the AI race.
